The present revision petition under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner/complainant against the order dated 05.09.2018, passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Jaitaran, District Pali whereby the learned Judge allowed the revision filed by accused-respondents No.2 to 4 and set aside the order dated 21.09.2016 passed by learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jaitaran, District Pali whereby the learned Magistrate took cognizance against the accused-respondent No.2 to 4 for offence under Section 420 & 406 IPC.
[2024:RJ-JD:45424] (2 of 4) [CRLR-1275/2018

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Jaitaran, District Pali
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ] Counsel for the petitioner submits that the learned revisional court has committed gross error in setting aside the order of cognizance passed by the trial court against the accused- respondents No.2 to 4 for offence under Sections 406 & 420 IPC as there is ample evidence against them for committing criminal breach of trust.

Counsel submits that certain amount of money was still owed to the Samiti and no justification/explanation was tendered Shivram vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:45424) on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53482837/
1 by the accused-respondents with respect to the same.

Counsel submits that at the stage of taking cognizance, only prima facie case has to be seen and the learned Magistrate prima facie found justifiable ground for taking cognizance against the accused-respondents for aforesaid offence, but the learned revisional court did not abide by the said principle and wrongly set aside the order of cognizance.
Thus, the order of revisional court deserves to be quashed and set aside.

Learned counsel for the respondents No.2 to 4 have opposed the prayer made by the counsel for the petitioner and submitted that initially after investigation, Police filed final report in the matter against the accused-respondents, against which the petitioner filed a protest petition, which was allowed by the learned trial Court and cognizance was taken against the accused- respondents for offence under Sections 420 & 406 IPC.
Against the order of cognizance, the accused-respondents filed a revision, which was allowed by the revisonal court.
Counsel submits that learned revisoinal court has considered each and every aspect of the matter and rightly passed the order.
The order of revisional court is a detailed reasoned order and thus, the same does not warrant any interference from this Court.
[2024:RJ-JD:45424] (3 of 4) [CRLR-1275/2018] Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the order impugned as well as material available on record.

Initially the police had filed the final report in the matter and subsequently on a protest petition being filed by the petitioner, the trial court took cognizance against the accused-respondents No.2 to 4 for offence under Section 406 & 420 IPC.
Against the order of cognizance, the accused-respondents filed a revision, which was allowed by the revisional court.
The Criminal Procedure Code provides for separate procedures for cases in which the cognizance has been taken on a complaint and on a police report.

It is provided under the code that if the learned Magistrate agrees with the police report he may proceed by accepting the police report dropping the proceeding but in case he is satisfied that upon the material collected by the police,
there is sufficient ground to proceed by rejecting the final report, can issue process straightway to the accused without being bound by the conclusions of the investigating agency,.
On perusal of the impugned revisional order, it is apparent that the revisional court has passed a detailed reasoned order considering each and every aspect of the matter.

The learned revisional court while setting aside the order of cognizance has observed that there is no evidence against the accused- respondents that they did embezzlement by using the money for their personal purpose and there is ample reasons with the accused-respondents for not deposing the money in dispute in the bank account and further, the audit report of the Samiti also did not shows any financial irregularities.
Thus, the alleged offences are not found to be proved against the accused-respondents.

[2024:RJ-JD:45424] (4 of 4) [CRLR-1275/2018] The learned revisonal court, after considering all the facts and circumstances of the case as well as material available on record has rightly set aside the order of cognizance passed by the trial court against the accused-respondents for offence under Section 406 & 420 IPC.

2
In the facts and circumstances of the case, no interference is called for in the impugned revisional order.
The revision petition is dismissed.
Stay application is also dismissed.

Record of the trial court be sent back immediately.
(MANOJ KUMAR GARG),J 142-MS/-
